expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'are you sure?' modal as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: "An 'are you sure?' modal is highly susceptible to click-through blindness."

expectations.text: Explains habituation or click-through blindness as why frequent dialogs stop working
expectations.evidence: "Users see these dialogs so often that they dismiss them reflexively without reading"

expectations.text: Recommends reversibility (soft delete with a retention window) as the strongest option
expectations.evidence: "implement a soft-delete (a trash/recycle bin with a retention period, e.g., 30 days)" as option 1

expectations.text: Recommends grace-period undo as a strong low-friction option
Recommends type-the-workspace-name confirmation for the irreversible case
expectations.evidence: "Type-to-confirm (Warning - Rung 2)...require an action proportional to the blast radius. A modal that asks the user to type the exact workspace name"

expectations.text: If a dialog is retained, requires it to name the workspace and the scale of what is lost
expectations.evidence: "'Delete workspace 'production-api' permanently? This will destroy 1,204 files.' The button must be labeled 'Delete forever'"

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the deletion rules, not just the UI
Gives an explicit preference order rather than an undifferentiated list of ideas
expectations.evidence: Clear numbered list: 1. Make it reversible, 2. Grace-period undo, 3. Type-to-confirm, 4. Specific consequence dialog
